_readme: Every African pre-travel authorisation scheme, one row each. A field with a null value means NOT YET ESTABLISHED, and renders as a gap. Never guess. Every non-null claim needs a source id resolving in data/sources.json.

schemes.name: EASE pre-registration + Airport Security Tax (TSA)
schemes.scope_note: Every foreign air traveller, including the visa-exempt. Cabo Verdean nationals, people born in Cabo Verde and legal residents are exempt. ECOWAS citizens are visa-exempt yet must still complete it.
schemes.compulsory_for: All foreign air travellers over two years old

fee.note: Airport Security Tax, roughly EUR31, reported by secondary sources. Confirm on ease.gov.cv.

schemes.refusable_note: Described as pre-registration rather than permission, and applications are 'approved', but whether one can be refused is not established.
schemes.avoi_treatment: Not established. This is the open question: Cabo Verde imposes a paid, mandatory pre-departure authorisation on visa-exempt African travellers and does not appear to have been classified the way Seychelles was.
needs: Confirm the TSA amount and whether it varies by nationality
Whether an EASE application can be refused
Whether it can be completed on arrival at all, or whether pre-departure is mandatory
schemes.notes: Predates Seychelles by four years and is the earliest African pre-travel authorisation found so far. Also suspended visa-on-arrival for 96 nationalities from 1 January 2026. The authorisation is valid for a year, unlike Seychelles' single-trip window. Whether it can be completed on arrival is NOT established, the consular portal directs travellers to pre-register up to five days before travel, and carriers check before boarding. Assume it must be done in advance.

schemes.name: Electronic Travel Authorisation (free)
schemes.scope_note: Mandatory for nationals of African Union member states who are NOT ECOWAS or AES members, and for other nationalities that were previously visa-exempt. ECOWAS and AES nationals, including Nigerians, are exempt and continue to enter visa-free with a valid passport.
schemes.compulsory_for: AU nationals outside ECOWAS and AES; previously visa-exempt non-African nationalities

fee.note: The ETA is issued free of charge. Separately, eVisas for visa-required nationals cost USD260 single entry and USD468 multiple entry, with fees waived for African nationals travelling for business or tourism.

schemes.refusable_note: Not established. Visa on arrival was discontinued on 25 May 2026, so there is no fallback at the border.
schemes.operator: Ghana Immigration Service with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
schemes.avoi_treatment: Introduced after the 2025 collection window, so not yet assessed. Under the published methodology a compulsory pre-travel authorisation scores zero regardless of cost, and visa on arrival scores 0.8. Ghana replaced the second with the first for non-ECOWAS Africans.
needs: Whether the ETA can be refused, and on what grounds
Stated processing time and minimum lead time
Whether AES nationals remain exempt given the ECOWAS withdrawals
schemes.notes: RESOLVED 15 August 2026. Widely reported as Ghana becoming the fifth country visa-free to all Africans. The mechanism is different: a mandatory free ETA before travel for AU nationals outside ECOWAS and AES, with visa on arrival discontinued. Free, which is what the AVOI recommends for such authorisations. But a compulsory pre-travel requirement scores zero on that index whatever it costs, so Ghana may be recorded as less open despite removing every fee. RE-CHECKED 13 OCTOBER 2026: no change found. The free ETA for AU nationals outside ECOWAS and AES is still as described.

schemes.name: Electronic Travel Authorisation
schemes.scope_note: eTA exemption granted to all African countries except Somalia and Libya, by Cabinet decision in January 2025. Most African visitors receive two months; East African Community nationals six months under EAC free movement protocols. Separately, a Health Ministry notice of 30 July 2026 requires foreign visitors staying under 12 months, Africans included, to hold travel health insurance of at least USD50,000. The High Court suspended it on 24 August 2026 and the case is still in court, so it is not being enforced for now.
schemes.compulsory_for: Nationals of Somalia and Libya, and non-African nationalities

fee.note: Fee position after the waiver not yet established.

schemes.refusable_note: Processing capped at 72 hours, with an expedited option offering instant approval.
schemes.avoi_treatment: Previously classified as a visa ahead of travel, ranking 46th. The waiver moved Kenya up 43 places.
needs: Whether any fee survives for Somali and Libyan nationals
Outcome of the High Court case on the USD50,000 visitor health insurance rule (hearing set for 16 September 2026, no ruling found yet)
schemes.notes: The closest thing to a natural experiment on the continent: same country, same borders, ETA on and ETA off, 43 places apart. Since this research, Somalia (from 1 September 2025) and Mauritania (from January 2025) have each launched their own mandatory eVisa/eTAS systems, Kenya's exclusion of Somalia and Libya from its waiver runs in one direction only; Somalia now separately requires an eVisa of everyone, Kenyans included. UPDATE 24 SEPTEMBER 2026: the ETA waiver for Africans still stands. A new USD50,000 travel health insurance rule for all foreign visitors (Gazette Notice 11492, 30 July 2026) was suspended by the High Court on 24 August 2026. Watch the court outcome: if the rule comes back, it would add a pre-travel step for African visitors even without an ETA.

schemes.name: Temporary Electronic Travel Authorisation
schemes.scope_note: Applied to nationals of eight countries who normally enter visa-free, for the duration of the Africa Cup of Nations.
schemes.compulsory_for: Nationals of eight visa-free countries, during the tournament period
needs: The eight countries
Whether it has in fact lapsed
Whether Morocco intends to make it permanent
schemes.notes: Ran roughly September 2025 to January 2026 for AFCON. The first African example of a temporary, event-driven authorisation imposed on visa-free travellers, a template worth watching for future tournaments.

schemes.name: Autorização Eletrónica de Viagem
schemes.scope_note: 29 countries. Only three are African: Ghana, Côte d'Ivoire and Senegal. The rest are European, North American, Middle Eastern or Asian.
schemes.compulsory_for: Nationals of the 29 listed countries

fee.note: An administration fee is reported but has not been confirmed on the portal.

schemes.avoi_treatment: Suspended at the time of the 2025 report, and recorded as having no effect on Mozambique's score.
needs: Administration fee amount
Official reinstatement date from SENAMI
Basis for the six-nationality online exclusion
schemes.notes: Announced April 2025, suspended 16 May 2025 over technical failures, rebuilt with VFS Global and operating again. Six nationalities, three of them African, cannot apply online at all and must attend an embassy. RE-CHECKED 13 OCTOBER 2026: no new notice found. Wikipedia still lists the ETA (USD 48) for the 29 countries; a wider search found no official reinstatement notice after the May 2025 suspension, so the reinstatement date is still open.

schemes.name: None found, visa on arrival, no pre-travel authorisation
schemes.scope_note: No ETA found. Around 22 nationalities enter visa-free, mostly SADC members. African nationals not on that list are covered by a visa-on-arrival policy introduced in 2024. Visa exemptions for 33 mainly Western nationalities ended on 1 April 2025 on reciprocity grounds.
schemes.compulsory_for: Nothing before travel
schemes.optional_for: Online application available before departure but not required

fee.note: Visa on arrival fee not yet established.

schemes.operator: Ministry of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security
schemes.avoi_treatment: No pre-travel authorisation. Visa on arrival would fall in the middle category.
needs: Confirm the AU visa-on-arrival policy scope with the Ministry
Visa on arrival fee
Confirm the current visa-free list
schemes.notes: Namibia moved the other way from most of the tracker: it removed exemptions for Western nationalities on reciprocity grounds while keeping and extending access for Africans. The KAZA UniVisa covering Zimbabwe and Zambia has been signed but not implemented by Namibia and Botswana.

schemes.name: Mandatory e-Visa (replaced visa on arrival)
schemes.scope_note: All nationalities that require a visa. ECOWAS citizens remain visa-free and are unaffected. All visitors, including ECOWAS and other visa-free nationals, must also fill in an online landing and exit card before arriving and before leaving (lecard.immigration.gov.ng).
schemes.compulsory_for: Every traveller who previously used visa on arrival

fee.note: Fee schedule varies by nationality and is set partly on a reciprocity basis. Figures circulating online are inconsistent, take them from the NIS portal only.

schemes.refusable_note: Applications are screened against international databases before approval; airlines can deny boarding without an approval email.
schemes.avoi_treatment: Recorded as one of four countries that moved from broad visa on arrival to requiring a visa ahead of travel. The report's West Africa section puts Nigeria at 32nd, down from 6th.
needs: e-Visa fee schedule from the NIS portal, by nationality
Stated processing time and whether it is met in practice
Reconcile the report's 32nd placing against its own country table, which appears to differ
Nigeria's AVOI 2025 score
Whether the landing and exit card is checked at boarding, and what happens to a traveller who arrives without one
schemes.notes: The subject of the first piece in this series. Announced 21 February 2025, visa on arrival phased out from 1 May 2025, Nigeria Visa Policy 2025 introduced that month. Framed as security and efficiency modernisation. Henley currently scores Nigeria 83rd in the world, admitting 19 of 198 nationalities without a prior visa, the two indices agree here, unlike Seychelles and Guinea-Bissau. Nigeria is also the nationality most often carved out elsewhere: barred from Mozambique's online channel, placed in Tanzania's Referral Visa category until 25 September 2026, and excluded from Tanzania's Commonwealth waiver. UPDATE 24 SEPTEMBER 2026: added the mandatory landing and exit card, in place since May 2025. It applies to every visitor, so it is the one pre-travel step that also reaches ECOWAS citizens who need no visa.

schemes.name: None, visa on arrival, no pre-travel step
schemes.scope_note: Checked and no pre-travel authorisation found. Visas are issued at the border post, free of charge for African Union, Commonwealth and Francophonie nationals.
schemes.compulsory_for: Nothing before travel
schemes.optional_for: Online application is available but not required; applicants may pay online or on arrival

fee.note: Free on arrival for AU, Commonwealth and Francophonie nationals.

schemes.operator: Directorate General of Immigration and Emigration
schemes.avoi_treatment: Joint first. No pre-travel requirement to classify.
needs: Re-check periodically, the value of this row is that it stays empty
schemes.notes: Recorded deliberately as a negative finding. Rwanda is the country most often held up as the model, and the check confirms there is no online step hiding behind the reputation. Useful as the control against which the others are read.

schemes.name: Travel Authorisation (eTA)
schemes.scope_note: Every non-citizen, regardless of nationality. The first African country to require one universally.
schemes.compulsory_for: Everyone

fee.note: Payment by card is required; the amount has not yet been sourced from the portal.

schemes.refusable_note: The consent screen states the data is processed for determining eligibility to travel, which implies a decision. Whether applications are in fact refused, and how often, is unanswered. Request filed under the Access to Information Act 2018.
schemes.avoi_treatment: Classified as an e-Visa, i.e. a visa required ahead of travel.
needs: Fee amount
Whether applications can be refused, and refusal counts
schemes.notes: Went from joint 1st in the 2024 AVOI to 54th of 54 in 2025 without refusing any African traveller. The single most consequential ETA on the continent for measurement purposes.

schemes.name: Electronic Travel Authorisation
schemes.scope_note: Rolling out in phases. As of the latest published update the ETA applies to nationals of Mainland China, India, Indonesia and Mexico, entering through OR Tambo, Cape Town, King Shaka (Durban) or Lanseria. NO AFRICAN NATIONALITY IS CURRENTLY IN SCOPE. The stated plan is to extend it to all visa-required countries and to the busiest land ports, including Beitbridge, Lebombo, Kopfontein, Skilpadhek and Maseru Bridge. The 22 African countries with visa exemptions remain outside it, described in the gazette as 'initially' optional.
schemes.compulsory_for: Nationals of China, India, Indonesia and Mexico at four airports. Extension to all visa-required countries announced.
schemes.optional_for: Nationals of visa-exempt countries, described in the gazette as 'initially' optional

fee.note: CONFIRMED IN FORCE. The Department of Home Affairs published the final fee regulation in Government Gazette 55209 on 17 August 2026, and the amendment took effect on publication. Applies to the same four nationalities already in scope (China, India, Indonesia, Mexico); visa-exempt travellers may optionally apply for an ETA at the same R500. No African nationality is in scope for the fee.

schemes.refusable_note: Travellers who require an ETA or eVisa and arrive without one cannot obtain one on arrival and are denied entry.
schemes.operator: State-operated; the proposal replaces an outsourced provider
schemes.avoi_treatment: Described in the 2025 report as materially different from other ETAs, because it replaces a consular visa process rather than adding a step for visa-free travellers, and as easing the travel experience.
needs: Whether the R500 also applies to work, business and permanent residence applications online
When African nationalities enter scope, and whether visa-exempt Africans become compulsory
The current ETA fee, which Fragomen reports is set on reciprocal visa fee arrangements and is not published

DISCREPANCY: some July 2026 reporting lists 32 African countries as visa-exempt for South Africa, including Nigeria, Ghana, Egypt and Ethiopia. Other reporting gives a much shorter ordinary-passport list. The longer list may relate to diplomatic and official passports. Resolve against the DHA schedule before using either.
Track the announced extension of the ETA to all visa-required countries and land ports, and re-check whether any African nationality enters scope
schemes.notes: UPDATE 8 SEPTEMBER 2026: The R500 fee is now confirmed in force, not merely proposed, per Government Gazette 55209 (17 August 2026). Re-verify interval relaxed from 7 to 30 days now that the core commencement question is resolved; the open question going forward is the announced rollout to all visa-required countries and additional land ports, and whether African nationalities enter scope. IMPORTANT SCOPE NOTE (unchanged): the ETA still does not apply to any African nationality. Coverage that framed the R500 as a charge on African travellers remains wrong. RE-CHECKED 13 SEPTEMBER 2026: no change. September news coverage still frames the wider rollout to more visa-required countries and land ports as an announced target, not yet executed; the live portal (eta.dha.gov.za) was in scheduled maintenance at check time and could not be inspected directly. No African nationality is newly in scope. RE-CHECKED 19 SEPTEMBER 2026: no African nationality newly in scope. The portal has accepted optional applications from visa-exempt nationals since 17 August 2026 (the R500 fee applies), and King Shaka Airport in Durban is planned as a fourth airport but was not yet live. Government reporting still gives extension to all visa-required countries in September 2026 as a target, not a confirmed event; the live portal could not be read directly. RE-CHECKED 24 SEPTEMBER 2026: King Shaka Airport in Durban is now reported as live, so the ETA runs at four airports (OR Tambo, Cape Town, King Shaka, Lanseria). Still only China, India, Indonesia and Mexico in scope, and no African nationality. Extension to all visa-required countries is still a target, not done. RE-CHECKED 13 OCTOBER 2026: Wikipedia now says the ETA is 'available for all visa-required countries' as of September 2026, but gives no source, and Fragomen (updated 18 August 2026) still names only China, India, Indonesia and Mexico, with no date set for the wider rollout. The portal could not be read directly. No African nationality is confirmed in scope, so nothing changes for travellers.

schemes.name: None, visa on arrival and e-Visa, no pre-travel authorisation
schemes.scope_note: Checked and no ETA found. EAC members, SADC members except Comoros, and Commonwealth countries except the UK, Canada, Nigeria, India, Pakistan, Australia and New Zealand enter without a visa. Others use an e-Visa or a visa on arrival.
schemes.compulsory_for: Nothing before travel for visa-exempt nationalities
schemes.optional_for: Online application available to all; recommended but not required for those eligible on arrival

fee.note: Ordinary visa. Business 250, multiple entry 100, transit 30. Nothing for visa-exempt nationalities.

schemes.refusable_note: Explicitly so. The guidelines state that a Visa Grant Notice is not final authority to enter, and an immigration officer at the entry point may still refuse.
schemes.avoi_treatment: No pre-travel authorisation to classify.
needs: Whether any separate arrival or customs declaration must be filed before departure
Tanzania's AVOI 2025 score and rank
The full, current Referral Visa country list
schemes.notes: No ETA, but Tanzania operates a differential access tier that no openness measure captures: the Referral Visa category (online application only, approval by the Commissioner General before travel, advised at least two months ahead, usually with an invitation letter from a host in Tanzania). Nigeria was in this category until 25 September 2026, when a public notice (Government Gazette No. 246 of 2026) removed it with immediate effect. Nigerians now use the ordinary visa, online or at the point of entry, USD 50. Nigeria is still one of seven Commonwealth countries excluded from the Commonwealth visa waiver, so it still needs a visa. From 1 October 2026 (Government Notice No. 256 of 2026) foreign visitors to mainland Tanzania must hold USD 44 NIC inbound travel insurance, bought online or on arrival; residents of EAC and SADC states are exempt. Zanzibar has had its own equivalent since October 2024.

schemes.name: None, visa-free for all African nationals
schemes.scope_note: PARTIALLY CONFIRMED. Popular coverage and The Gambia's own formal visa policy do not fully agree on scope. The AVOI scores The Gambia 1.000 and joint first, indicating visa-free access for citizens of all 53 other African countries, but this has not been confirmed against the Gambia Immigration Department directly.
schemes.compulsory_for: Nothing before travel

fee.note: No fee for African nationals.

schemes.avoi_treatment: Joint first with Rwanda. Nothing to classify.
needs: Confirm scope directly with the Gambia Immigration Department
Reconcile the formal visa policy against the index score
Establish whether any category of African traveller is excluded
schemes.notes: Held as partially confirmed deliberately. This is a genuinely open question rather than a gap we have not got to. Recorded alongside Rwanda as a control, but with less confidence than Rwanda, which was confirmed from its immigration directorate.

schemes.name: Possible ETA requirement, unverified
schemes.scope_note: CONFLICTING INFORMATION. The 2025 AVOI recorded Zambia as considering an advance passenger information system with an authorisation attached. A travel advisory service reports that Zambia now requires an ETA of most visitors including transit passengers. Neither has been confirmed against the Zambian Department of Immigration. Treat as unresolved and check before travelling.
needs: PRIORITY: establish whether an ETA requirement is actually in force, from zambiaimmigration.gov.zm
If in force: scope, fee, lead time, and whether transit passengers are included
schemes.notes: UPDATE 8 SEPTEMBER 2026: Checked the official Zambia Department of Immigration site directly per the 'needs' note below. It makes no mention of an Electronic Travel Authorization anywhere; only e-Visa, visa-free entry for 53 countries, and standard permits are described. This does not conclusively rule out a requirement (a government site can lag reality) but it weighs against the only source claiming a live requirement, which is the same class of commercial travel-advisory source this project has already found unreliable elsewhere (see Libya). Status held at 'proposed' rather than downgraded or upgraded, pending an unambiguous government statement either way. RE-CHECKED 13 SEPTEMBER 2026: same result, still no ETA section on the official site and no newer government statement found either way. RE-CHECKED 19 SEPTEMBER 2026: the official 'For Visitors' page on zambiaimmigration.gov.zm still describes only the e-Visa and the 53-country visa waiver, with no ETA anywhere, and a wider search found no government or credible-outlet statement of an ETA requirement. Status unchanged. RE-CHECKED 13 OCTOBER 2026: still no government or credible-outlet statement of a Zambian ETA requirement; the only trace remains the 2025 AVOI report that one was being considered. Status unchanged.

schemes.name: None found, eVisa system, no separate pre-travel authorisation
schemes.scope_note: No ETA found. Zimbabwe's eVisa platform lists 17 African countries as visa-free: Angola, Botswana, DR Congo, Ghana, Kenya, Lesotho, Madagascar, Malawi, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, Seychelles, South Africa, Eswatini, Uganda and others. Nigeria is not on the list. Others use an eVisa or a visa on arrival.
schemes.compulsory_for: Nothing before travel for the 17 listed African nationalities
schemes.optional_for: eVisa available as an alternative to visa on arrival

fee.note: eVisa fees vary by category and nationality. Not yet established.

schemes.avoi_treatment: No pre-travel authorisation to classify. The eVisa would score as a pre-travel requirement for nationalities that need one.
needs: Confirm the 17-country list directly on evisa.gov.zw
eVisa fee schedule by nationality
Processing time, reported as around seven working days
schemes.notes: Nigeria is absent from Zimbabwe's visa-free list, making this the third country in the tracker where Nigerian travellers face a materially different route from their neighbours. Separately, Zimbabwean citizens now require an eTA for Ghana and Seychelles, which independently corroborates that Ghana's new authorisation captures non-ECOWAS African nationals.

schemes.name: None found, traditional consular visa, small African exemption list
schemes.scope_note: Checked. No ETA or e-Visa open to African nationals was found. A small number of African neighbours (reported as roughly six or seven countries, including Libya, Mali, Mauritania, Morocco, Seychelles and Tunisia) enter visa-free or with permission on arrival. All other African nationalities must apply for a traditional visa in person at an Algerian embassy or consulate before travel. Algeria does run an eVisa portal, but reporting indicates it is currently limited to a short list of non-African nationalities (EU/Schengen, US, Canada, Gulf states), not to Africans generally.
schemes.compulsory_for: Traditional consular visa for African nationalities not on the small exemption list

fee.note: Not established for African nationalities; embassy visa fees vary.

schemes.avoi_treatment: No pre-travel authorisation to classify; the traditional consular-visa requirement for most Africans is reflected in Algeria's low AVOI score.
needs: Confirm the exact list of visa-exempt African countries directly with an Algerian embassy
Whether Algeria's eVisa portal has been or will be extended to African nationalities
Fee and processing time for the ordinary consular visa
schemes.notes: Distinct from Morocco's temporary AEVM scheme, under which Algerian citizens themselves needed a travel authorisation for AFCON 2025, that scheme concerned Algerians travelling to Morocco, not travel into Algeria.

schemes.name: Mandatory online e-visa (pre-visa) for non-exempt nationalities
schemes.scope_note: Angola grants 90-day visa-free tourist entry to 14 named African countries (Tanzania, Eswatini, Morocco, Lesotho, Rwanda, Zimbabwe, Equatorial Guinea, Botswana, Madagascar, Malawi, Mauritius, Seychelles, Cape Verde, Algeria) under a 2023 presidential decree. All other African nationalities must obtain Angola's online e-visa/pre-visa before travel; work, study and business visas always require advance application regardless of nationality.
schemes.compulsory_for: African nationalities outside the 14-country visa-free list, for any purpose beyond visa-exempt tourism

fee.note: Reported around USD120 payable on arrival for some categories; not confirmed for the standard tourist e-visa. Confirm on the Angolan e-visa portal.

schemes.operator: Serviço de Migração e Estrangeiros (SME), Ministry of the Interior
schemes.avoi_treatment: A mandatory e-visa for non-exempt nationalities scores as a pre-travel requirement; the 14-country visa-free list improves Angola's regional score.
needs: Confirm current e-visa fee and processing time from the official Angolan portal
Whether the 14-country visa-free list has changed since 2023
Whether any other African nationalities have since been added to the exempt list
schemes.notes: Angola moved from a highly restrictive visa regime to one of the more open ones on the continent within a few years, though most African nationalities still route through the mandatory e-visa rather than enjoying the visa-free list.

schemes.name: ECOWAS free movement; status for non-ECOWAS travellers not yet established
schemes.scope_note: Citizens of the 12 ECOWAS member states enter visa-free under the 1979 free movement protocol, typically for up to 90 days. What is required of NON-ECOWAS African travellers has not been established for this country. Do not assume nothing is required.
schemes.compulsory_for: Nothing for ECOWAS citizens. Not established for other nationalities.

fee.note: No fee for ECOWAS citizens. Fees for other nationalities not established.

schemes.avoi_treatment: ECOWAS holds the highest average score of any regional economic community at 0.597, down from 0.629 in 2024.
needs: PRIORITY: establish what non-ECOWAS African travellers require
Whether any online pre-travel step exists
Fees and processing times for non-ECOWAS nationalities
schemes.notes: Benin was joint first on the 2024 AVOI, visa-free to all African countries. Reporting from July 2026 indicates it has since published a narrower list of around 11 non-ECOWAS African countries with waivers, with six more limited to diplomatic and service passports. If accurate this is a significant narrowing and needs verifying urgently.

schemes.name: None found, visa-free list, visa required for others
schemes.scope_note: No pre-travel authorisation found. Fifteen African countries are reported visa-exempt: South Africa, Zimbabwe, Zambia, Tanzania, Uganda, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, Lesotho, Eswatini, Sierra Leone, The Gambia, Seychelles and Mauritius. Citizens of other African countries must complete a formal visa application before arrival.
schemes.compulsory_for: Nothing for the 15 exempt nationalities. A visa before arrival for other Africans.

fee.note: Not established.

schemes.avoi_treatment: A visa required before arrival scores as a pre-travel requirement for the nationalities affected.
needs: Confirm the 15-country list with Botswana immigration
Whether an online application channel exists, and whether any nationality is excluded from it
Visa fees and processing times
schemes.notes: Nigeria is not among the 15 exempt nationalities. The KAZA UniVisa, which would cover Botswana alongside Zimbabwe, Zambia and Namibia, has been signed but not implemented by Botswana.

schemes.name: Mandatory online visa, fee waived for African nationals since Sept 2025
schemes.scope_note: ECOWAS and AES nationals enter visa-free under free-movement protocols (confirmed still in force via the December 2024 Bamako declaration). All other African nationals must apply and be approved online via visaburkina.bf before travel; since a September 2025 Council of Ministers decision the fee for approved African applicants has been waived, but officials stressed 'free is not the same as exempt', the online application and approval step remains compulsory.
schemes.compulsory_for: Non-ECOWAS/AES African nationals, and other nationalities not on the visa-exempt list

fee.note: Free for African nationals since the September 2025 decision, provided the online application via visaburkina.bf is submitted and approved. Non-African visa-required nationals pay the standard eVisa fee.

schemes.refusable_note: Applications are reviewed before being approved; the government describes the waiver as fee-free, not visa-free.
schemes.operator: Direction Générale de la Police Nationale / visaburkina.bf portal
schemes.avoi_treatment: A mandatory online pre-travel approval, even at zero cost, scores as a pre-travel authorisation requirement rather than visa-free access.
needs: Confirm processing time for the free African-national visa channel
Whether AES states (Mali, Niger) extend a reciprocal fee waiver
Whether the fee waiver has since been formalised in a published decree
schemes.notes: A close cousin of Ghana's May 2026 reform: a nominally 'free' mandatory pre-travel approval, which the AVOI methodology would still score as a pre-travel requirement rather than true visa-free access.

schemes.name: All-Africa waiver claim contradicted by two government sources; narrower EAC-only exemption confirmed
schemes.scope_note: UPDATED 13 SEPTEMBER 2026. Two Burundian government-affiliated sources, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' free-visa page and the Burundi Embassy in Turkey's exemption list, both directly contradict the May 2026 blog's claim of an all-Africa waiver: the embassy page names only Democratic Republic of Congo, Rwanda, Uganda, Tanzania and Kenya as visa-exempt, and the ministry page limits fee waivers to EAC and CEPGL member nationals, EAC students, and diplomats. Note the embassy's 5-country list omits South Sudan, which earlier compilations included as a 6th EAC member exempt from Burundian visas, that discrepancy is not yet resolved. A mandatory e-Visa (immigration.gov.bi) still applies to non-exempt nationalities, including most non-EAC Africans.
schemes.compulsory_for: Nothing for the 5 exempt EAC-region nationalities named by the embassy source. Required for other African nationalities, including possibly South Sudan pending the discrepancy above.

fee.note: e-Visa reported around USD40 (single entry) to USD90 (multiple entry) for non-exempt nationalities, pending confirmation of whether this still applies to non-EAC Africans.

schemes.avoi_treatment: Burundi's high 2025 AVOI score (0.823, rank 9) predates the alleged May 2026 all-Africa waiver, which is now contradicted by government sources rather than confirmed, so the score is not expected to change on this basis.
needs: Reconcile the embassy's 5-country exempt list against the 6-member EAC roster (South Sudan's status specifically)
Current e-Visa fee and process for non-EAC Africans, confirmed directly rather than via the still-unconfirmed USD40-90 range
Whether Somalia's 2024 EAC accession has any bearing on Burundian visa exemption (not mentioned by either new source)
schemes.notes: The all-Africa waiver claim is now treated as effectively debunked, two independent Burundian government-affiliated pages (checked 2026-09-13) describe only a narrow EAC/CEPGL exemption, not a continent-wide one. Re-verify interval relaxed from 30 to 90 days now that the high-stakes contradiction is resolved; the open question going forward is the exact exempt-country count, not whether a blanket waiver exists.

schemes.name: Mandatory eVisa, small CEMAC/bilateral exemption list
schemes.scope_note: Nearly all foreign visitors, including most African nationalities, must obtain a mandatory eVisa before travel. Reporting indicates a small visa-exempt list of CEMAC members (Chad, Central African Republic, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Congo) plus Nigeria and Mali.
schemes.compulsory_for: African nationalities outside the small exempt list

fee.note: Not established; fees vary by nationality and visa type.

schemes.operator: Direction Générale de la Sûreté Nationale (eVisa portal)
schemes.avoi_treatment: A mandatory eVisa for most non-exempt Africans is consistent with Cameroon's low AVOI score.

schemes.avoi_treatment: Senegal's relatively high AVOI score (0.792, rank 14) reflects broad visa-free ECOWAS and bilateral access; the e-Visa applies mainly to nationalities outside that broad exemption.
needs: Confirm whether non-ECOWAS Africans specifically are required to pre-enrol online or can still rely on visa on arrival
e-Visa fee and processing time from a primary Senegalese government source
schemes.notes: TERTIARY sourcing, the co-existence of a mandatory-in-practice e-Visa and a genuine on-arrival fallback makes Senegal a softer case than Togo or Côte d'Ivoire; verify before citing as fully mandatory.

schemes.name: None (for African Union citizens), visa on arrival covers all AU nationals
schemes.scope_note: Beyond ECOWAS free movement, Sierra Leone extends visa on arrival to African Union citizens generally: free for Botswana, Eswatini, Kenya, Lesotho, Malawi and Mauritius, and USD25 for other AU nationals. Only non-AU nationalities are directed to an e-Visa. This resolves the earlier 'not verified' status, no pre-travel authorisation is required of African travellers.
schemes.compulsory_for: Nothing before travel for AU nationals; an e-Visa for non-AU nationalities

fee.note: Free visa on arrival for Botswana, Eswatini, Kenya, Lesotho, Malawi and Mauritius; USD25 visa on arrival for other AU nationals.

schemes.avoi_treatment: No pre-travel authorisation to classify for AU nationals; consistent with Sierra Leone's high AVOI score (0.811, rank 10).
needs: Confirm the fee list and free-VOA country list directly with Sierra Leonean immigration
Whether any online pre-registration is required alongside the on-arrival process
schemes.notes: TERTIARY sourcing (Wikipedia), a strong candidate for reclassification once confirmed against a primary government source, since it suggests Sierra Leone is materially more open to Africans than 'ECOWAS-only' entries elsewhere in this tracker.

schemes.name: Mandatory eVisa/eTAS for all foreign visitors
schemes.scope_note: Somalia's Electronic Visa and Travel Authorization System (eVisa/eTAS) launched 28 August 2025 and became mandatory for all foreign visitors, including infants and children, from 1 September 2025. No nationality exemptions have been reported so far.
schemes.compulsory_for: All foreign visitors, of any nationality including African

fee.note: Not established.

schemes.refusable_note: Applications are adjudicated through evisa.gov.so before an entry permit is issued.
schemes.operator: Immigration and Citizenship Agency (ICA) of Somalia
schemes.avoi_treatment: A universal mandatory pre-travel authorisation with no African exemptions scores at the bottom of the AVOI methodology; Somalia's 2025 score (0.185, rank 41) predates the September 2025 launch and will need re-assessment in the 2026 report.
needs: Confirm fee, processing time and any nationality exemptions since launch
Whether the AVOI score will be revised downward once the mandatory system is captured in the next report
schemes.notes: One of the most recent and comprehensive African pre-travel authorisation launches found in this research, Kenya's eTA exemption explicitly still excludes Somalia and Libya on security grounds, so a Somali eTAS traveller headed to Kenya faces a visa, while inbound to Somalia now faces a universal eVisa of its own. RE-CHECKED 13 OCTOBER 2026: no change found. The eVisa/eTAS is still described as mandatory for all visitors; sources still disagree on whether any nationality can get a visa on arrival.

schemes.name: Mandatory eVisa for most nationalities; Kenya and Tanzania exempt
schemes.scope_note: Kenya and Tanzania are visa-exempt for an indefinite period; a small number of other nationalities are eligible for visa on arrival. All other nationalities, which includes most African countries, must obtain an eVisa before travel, open to citizens of any country for single or multiple entry.
schemes.compulsory_for: African nationalities other than Kenya and Tanzania

fee.note: Not established.

schemes.operator: South Sudan Directorate of Nationality, Passports and Immigration
schemes.avoi_treatment: A mandatory eVisa for most non-exempt Africans is consistent with South Sudan's very low AVOI score (0.087, rank 51).
needs: Confirm the exact visa-on-arrival eligible nationalities
eVisa fee and processing time

schemes.name: None found, traditional advance visa; narrow on-arrival exemption for Eritrea, Kenya, Malaysia
schemes.scope_note: Sudan's civil war since April 2023 has disrupted normal immigration administration and Khartoum's main airport. Available reporting indicates only Eritrean, Kenyan and Malaysian nationals can get a visa on arrival, at Port Sudan International Airport specifically, subject to discretionary security screening. All other African nationalities must obtain a visa in advance from a Sudanese embassy or consulate; no e-Visa or ETA system was found. Treat this as a snapshot of a fluid, conflict-affected situation rather than settled policy.
schemes.compulsory_for: Advance embassy visa for African nationalities other than Eritrea, Kenya and Malaysia

fee.note: Reported roughly USD50 cash fee for the narrow on-arrival category (Eritrea, Kenya, Malaysia) at Port Sudan; embassy visa fees for other nationalities not established.

schemes.refusable_note: Even the narrow on-arrival category is subject to discretionary security assessment by immigration officials, not a guarantee.
schemes.operator: Sudanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs (embassies) / immigration at Port Sudan
schemes.avoi_treatment: Sudan's very low AVOI score (0.030, rank 53), the second-lowest on the continent, is consistent with a broadly restrictive regime independent of the conflict-related disruption documented here.
needs: Confirm current status against a government or UN source given the ongoing conflict
Whether any functioning e-Visa or online step has since been introduced
Whether other African nationalities have separate arrangements not captured in tertiary sources
schemes.notes: Short re-verify interval reflects the conflict-driven volatility rather than confidence in the finding; sourcing here is tertiary (Grokipedia) and should be treated as provisional pending a primary Sudanese government or embassy statement. RE-CHECKED 19 SEPTEMBER 2026: an embassy page (sudanembassy.org) still describes only postal or in-person applications with USD154 processing fees and no online system. One search summary claimed an e-visa exists but cited a commercial aggregator, not a government source, so it was not adopted. Status unchanged, sourcing still weaker than we would like.

schemes.name: Mandatory eVisa/embassy visa, small African exemption list
schemes.scope_note: Resolved: visitors must obtain a visa, either online through the eVisaST portal or from a São Toméan diplomatic mission, before arrival, unless they hold a passport from one of roughly eight visa-exempt countries (a 2015 policy covering, from Africa, Angola, Cape Verde and Equatorial Guinea, alongside the EU, US, Canada and Brazil) for stays up to 15 days. The AVOI 2025 report separately names São Tomé and Príncipe as one of the most restrictive ECCAS members toward fellow Central African states.
schemes.compulsory_for: Non-exempt African nationalities

fee.note: Not established; eVisa reported single-entry, valid 30 days from issue, stay up to 30 days.

schemes.operator: Government of São Tomé and Príncipe (eVisaST portal) / diplomatic missions
schemes.avoi_treatment: AVOI 2025 score 0.151, rank 44 (tied with Morocco), consistent with a mandatory pre-travel visa/eVisa for most African nationalities and with the ECCAS regional section naming it among the bloc's most restrictive members.
needs: Confirm the current exact exemption list and eVisa fee from the official eVisaST portal
Whether the eVisa is available to African nationalities outside the roughly eight-country exempt list, or whether they are pushed to embassy applications only
schemes.notes: Resolved from 'unchecked'; sourcing here is a tertiary Wikipedia/VisaHQ compilation rather than the eVisaST portal itself, so fee and lead-time details should be confirmed against the primary portal before being treated as settled.

schemes.name: Visa-free for Africans with a mandatory online immigration form (since 18 May 2026)
schemes.scope_note: Since 18 May 2026 all African nationals with a valid passport can enter Togo without a visa for up to 30 days, by land, air or sea. The condition is an online immigration form (bordereau d'immigration) at voyage.gouv.tg, completed at least 24 hours before arrival. Visa on arrival is currently suspended. Non-African nationals who need a visa still apply for an e-Visa on the same platform.
schemes.compulsory_for: All African nationals with a valid passport: online immigration form at least 24 hours before arrival. Other visa-required nationalities still need an e-Visa.

fee.note: The government portal and the reporting do not state a cost for the immigration form. e-Visa fees for non-African nationalities not established.

schemes.avoi_treatment: The 2025 AVOI score (0.283, rank 35) predates the 18 May 2026 exemption and reflects the old e-Visa regime for non-ECOWAS Africans, so it likely understates Togo's current openness. Not yet reassessed.
needs: Whether the immigration form costs anything
Whether ECOWAS nationals must also complete it
What happens if a traveller arrives without the form, and whether airlines check it at boarding
Confirm the non-African e-Visa fee and lead time from a government source (the five-business-day figure is from a tertiary source)
schemes.notes: UPDATED 19 SEPTEMBER 2026. Earlier versions of this entry said non-ECOWAS Africans needed a mandatory e-Visa; that stopped being true on 18 May 2026. Read the headline carefully: it is visa-free, but not 'nothing to do before you fly'. The immigration form is a compulsory pre-travel step, which is why this stays listed as an operating scheme. Confirmed on the government's own portal (voyage.gouv.tg).

schemes.name: Visa-free for ~22 African countries; eVisa platform delayed, no launch date
schemes.scope_note: Reporting indicates 22 African countries are visa-free for up to 90 days. Tunisia planned a national eVisa platform (African Development Bank-supported), but the tender launched in September 2024 was declared unsuccessful on 26 August 2025: none of eight bids met the requirements, and no new tender or launch date has been announced. Non-exempt nationalities still apply through a consulate or embassy.
schemes.compulsory_for: Consular visa for non-exempt nationalities. No online pre-travel step exists yet.

fee.note: Not established.

schemes.avoi_treatment: Not yet assessed for the eVisa; Tunisia's current AVOI score (0.377, rank 25) predates the platform going live.
needs: CHECK PERIODICALLY: whether a replacement eVisa tender is launched or a platform goes live
Confirm the exact 22-country visa-free list
Whether a future eVisa will apply to, or exempt, African nationalities specifically
schemes.notes: CORRECTED 19 SEPTEMBER 2026. This entry previously described the eVisa platform as 'rolling out' and held Tunisia at 'proposed'. The tender failed in August 2025 and nothing has replaced it, so there is no scheme to apply for. Status moved to 'none' until a platform is announced with a date.

schemes.name: Mandatory online e-Visa (no visa on arrival)
schemes.scope_note: All visa-required nationalities must apply online before travel. There is no visa on arrival. Citizens of East African Community member states, Kenya, Rwanda, Tanzania, Burundi and South Sudan, enter visa-free.
schemes.compulsory_for: All visa-required nationalities, which includes most African countries outside the EAC

fee.note: Single entry USD50; multiple entry USD100; East Africa Tourist Visa USD100. From secondary guides, confirm on visas.immigration.go.ug.

schemes.refusable_note: Applications are adjudicated and an approval letter is issued. Immigration officers retain authority to refuse entry at the port.
schemes.operator: Directorate of Citizenship and Immigration Control
schemes.avoi_treatment: An e-Visa required before travel scores as a pre-travel requirement.
needs: Confirm the fee schedule on visas.immigration.go.ug
Confirm which African nationalities are visa-exempt beyond the EAC
Whether airlines verify approval before boarding
schemes.notes: Same pattern as Nigeria: visa on arrival removed, permission moved online and before departure. Approval must be printed and presented; reporting indicates digital copies are not accepted at entry, which is worth confirming. A sixth African country where the moment of permission has moved. CHECKED 2 OCTOBER 2026 against the official visa-exempt list on immigration.go.ug: Mozambique is now on it (the 2024 agreement, reported in force from March 2026), and Angola is not, although Wikipedia still lists Angola. Shown to travellers as 'sources disagree' for Angola. The same site posted a notice on 2 October 2026 that a yellow fever vaccination certificate is no longer mandatory for entry.
